accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.body:
1. Commitment
KisaraUI is designed with accessibility in mind, and we aim for the node list, the input fields, reordering and adding nodes to be operable with the keyboard alone.

2. Scope
The screens of KisaraUI (the whole app running on this page). Content returned by the ComfyUI and LLM servers and services you connect to (generated images and text, node names, etc.) and the screens of those providers are not included.

3. Target and conformance status
We aim for WCAG 2.1 Level AA (JIS X 8341-3:2016 Level AA). However, conformance has not been verified or guaranteed. In the wording of the Web Accessibility Infrastructure Committee (WAIC) of Japan, this corresponds to "配慮" (taken into consideration).

4. How we check
During development we check that the app can be operated with the keyboard alone, using automated tests and validation tools.

5. Known limitations
- The links between nodes in a workflow are drawn as a picture; the picture itself is not read aloud. The connections can be followed through names and text.
- Images generated by the services you connect to are not described in text.

6. Feedback
Please send us anything that is hard to use through the contact form (https://contact.kisara-ui.com).

connection.remoteTitle: Notice on connecting to an external ComfyUI
connection.remoteNotice:
You are about to connect to a ComfyUI outside your own device or private network. Before connecting, please note:
- Running workflows uses that ComfyUI's GPU and changes its state.
- On paid hosting, the provider charges you based on usage time or runs. Checking the fees and managing how often, how long and at what cost you use it is up to you (Terms of Use, Article 4). We do not reimburse fees (Article 8).
- On a shared server, its administrator and other users may be able to see what you send and generate.
- Please use the server in line with its terms of use and applicable laws.
- Our liability for damage arising from your use of external servers is as set out in Article 11 of the Terms of Use.
If you agree, please connect.

connect.heading: Connect to ComfyUI
connect.launchNote: Add the launch option to the command that starts ComfyUI, as below.
connect.launchWhy: This UI runs locally in your browser, but with ComfyUI's default settings the browser's requests to another URL are blocked, so this option is required.
connect.securityCors: By default, ComfyUI tells the browser not to process requests from a different URL, so the enable-cors-header option is needed to add an exception.
connect.securityListen: enable-cors-header does not allow network access from other PCs or the internet. That requires exposing ComfyUI on the network with the --listen option, which is very risky; avoid it unless you have enough knowledge and a clear intention.
connect.securityDirect: KisaraUI runs in your local browser and sends what you enter directly from the browser to ComfyUI, so it is designed never to send what you run to an outside party or relay it.
connect.securityTamper: However, if inappropriate code were embedded in the page through tampering with the website or a malicious update, it would theoretically be possible to send information on the UI elsewhere or to extract information through the ComfyUI API.
connect.securityScope: In this way, the risk is limited to what the ComfyUI API can do. This is somewhat more secure than custom nodes, which can gain access to OS resources as part of the ComfyUI process, but please use it with an understanding of the potential risks.
connect.securityInspect: If these risks concern you, you can verify them, for example by checking where and what is sent with the browser's developer tools (F12), or by saving this page and having a generative AI analyze the code.

welcome.title: KisaraUI
welcome.about: KisaraUI is an API frontend for easily running LLM chat and image generation. It runs entirely in your browser and sends requests to your own AI runtime or to cloud APIs.
welcome.useChat: Connect to your own LLM server or to cloud APIs such as OpenRouter and chat.
welcome.useImage: Open workflows on your own ComfyUI, change values and run them.
welcome.featureBrowser: No installation of KisaraUI itself and no account sign-up are needed. Connect it to the LLM runtime or ComfyUI environment you already have.
welcome.featurePrivacy: Your browser communicates directly with your inference environment; what you send is never relayed and results are never sent elsewhere.
welcome.featureCraft: Simple to operate, while keeping what happens behind the scenes transparent and customizable.

webSearch.confirmDescription:
When the model decides it is needed, the connected cloud service is asked to search the web or fetch pages.
Each operation, such as a search or a fetch, incurs a set extra fee on top of tokens.

Some web pages contain far more text than they appear to, so a fetch may consume a large number of tokens, and repeated fetches may lead to high API charges.

When using this feature, set a spending limit and rate limits with the connected service, and manage your usage at your own responsibility by means other than the App as well, such as checking usage and billing status with the connected service.

The content of pages retrieved by web search enters the chat mixed into the responses. Do not put information you could not afford to have leaked into chats with web search enabled.

playbook.title: Playbook

story.name: Plot progression
story.description: Decide everything from the premise to the sections in one consultation and cut them into steps, choose whether to follow a plot or only fix the flow, and write one step at a time.
story.role: You are a co-writer working on a story with the person you are talking to. {{user}} is the protagonist of the story; {{user}} is not that person and not someone you talk to. Follow the way of writing decided in the plot consultation. For a story that follows the plot, keep the decided setting and beats and do not add big events that are not in the beats. For a story where only the flow is fixed, head for the goal of the enabled step while freely making the path and contents, and bring in unexpected events and choices of the characters. Either way, do not contradict the facts in the story so far and in the dictionaries, leave the ending to the person you are writing with and do not wrap the story up. Where that person needs to decide, ask instead of writing. Put anything that is not the story itself (replies to their instructions, ideas for what comes next, questions) in <comment> tags, apart from the story text.

writing.name: Plot progression
writing.goal: Create the plot in the sub-session, and select the chapter to write.

makePlan.name: Consult on the plot
makePlan.greeting:
We will decide the story from the premise to the sections, in order.
First, choose the way of writing: follow a plot (decide detailed beats for each section), or fix only the flow (sections have only goals, and the contents are left to each writing).
Also tell me the genre and mood, and any hints of scenes or characters you want. If you have a story structure in mind (four-part, three-act, hero's journey...), tell me that too.
makePlan.instruction:
This is the consultation for deciding the plot. Go through the steps below in order; propose for each step, and move on after the user applies it.
{{user}} is the protagonist of the story, not someone the narrator talks with. Never write entries that address {{user}} or describe the story as a dialogue with {{user}}.
0. Way of writing: let the user decide whether to follow a plot or to fix only the flow. If not decided, show in one line each what each suits (follow a plot: when you want a fixed structure; only the flow: when you want to enjoy unexpected turns) and ask. Make the decided way a constant individual dictionary entry (comment "Way of writing").
1. Premise: from the hints, offer 3-4 premises (one sentence each, with {{user}} as the protagonist, their want and the central conflict) in different directions, and let the user pick one. Do not write the ending. Make the chosen premise a constant individual dictionary entry.
2. Characters and setting: {{user}} is the protagonist, so do not create another protagonist. Create 2-4 other main characters (name, role, want, weakness, one sample line) and the setting (place, era, rules). Make the setting a constant individual dictionary entry, and each character an entry keyed by their name. Do not use currentSituation.
3. Outline: show the sections in the structure the user chose (four-part if none), with the goal of each and what has changed at its end, and confirm them. If only the flow is fixed, turn the agreed sections into outline steps one by one and finish here. In that case write in each step only its situation, its goal and what has changed at its end, not the events inside it.
4. Beats (only when following a plot): for each section, offer 2-4 detailed beats as candidates and let the user pick. Turn the chosen beats into outline steps one by one in writing order. Do not write the ending of the last section; the user decides it.

revise.name: Proofread the last reply
revise.instruction:
Reread the last passage as an editor and write it again with only the parts that need fixing changed. Check whether it reaches the beat or goal of the enabled step, whether a plot-following story adds events not in the beats, contradictions with the character settings, clichés, unnecessary exposition, purple prose, repeated words, habits in endings, and drift in tense and voice. Keep every sentence that needs no fix word for word, and write only the passage, with no explanation or preface.
<comment>Do not send this as a message. Press the regenerate icon and use it as the instruction for regenerating.</comment>

deepen.name: Deepen
deepen.instruction: Without moving on to the events of the next step or settling anything, stay in the current scene and deepen it. Thicken its texture with sensory detail, pauses and the characters’ inner state, and raise the tension, emotions or what is at stake by one notch. Use not only the exchange between characters but also the place, time pressure and what happens around them.

shake.name: Shake up
shake.instruction: Add one thing that keeps the story from going smoothly: an attempt toward the goal of the step that fails, an unexpected event, or a character’s doubt. Do not settle it.

shift.name: Switch
shift.instruction: Keep the goal of the step, and continue after switching the scene (place, time) or the character whose view tells it. Show the switch in one sentence.

widen.name: Widen
widen.instruction: Keep the direction of the story and the goal of the step, and add variation to the flow. Show it in a different form through another way toward the same goal, another character getting involved, or a small event within the scene. Do not add new obstacles or turning points, and end with at least one thing changed from before.

close.name: Head to the end
close.instruction: Write toward closing the current step. Bring the scene to a break so that it leads naturally into the next step ({{nextStep}}). Do not write the events of the next step yet.

story.continue: Continue the text right after the last passage, in the same style and point of view. Follow the way of writing decided in the plot consultation, and do not go beyond the beat or goal of the enabled step.

roleplay.name: Role-play
roleplay.description: Decide the setting, the relationship and the big flow in one consultation, and play step by step as {{char}}.
roleplay.role: You play scenes with {{user}} as {{char}}. Do not write the lines, actions or feelings of {{user}}. Keep the voice of the description and the dialogue examples, and move scenes toward the goal of the enabled step without getting ahead of the choices of {{user}}.

prepare.name: Preparation
prepare.goal: In the sub-session, decide the setting, the relationship between {{char}} and {{user}}, and the steps of the big flow.

scene.name: Scene
scene.goal: Select the step to move on in the outline and send what you say to {{char}}. Use the commands when you want to move the scene.

closing.name: Closing
closing.goal: Close the exchange of the section with the command "Close the scene", and review the voice and flow with "Check the voice".

makePlan.name: Decide setting and flow
makePlan.greeting:
Let's decide the setting of the role-play, the relationship between {{char}} and {{user}}, and the big flow, in order.
Tell me hints about the world and the situation you want to start in.
makePlan.instruction:
This is the preparation phase of this playbook. Go through the steps below in order; propose for each step, and move on after the user applies it.
1. Opening: from the hints, offer 3 opening situations with different moods and let the user pick one.
2. Setting and relationship: decide the setting, the relationship between {{char}} and {{user}}, what {{char}} wants now and what {{char}} hides. Put the character into the card fields, the setting and relationship into constant individual dictionary entries, and what is hidden into an entry keyed by related words. Do not use currentSituation.
3. Big flow: show the flow of the exchange in 3-5 sections, and turn the agreed sections into outline steps one by one. Write the opening situation into the first step. In each step write only its situation, how the relationship between {{char}} and {{user}} changes and which way {{char}} leans. Do not decide the actions of {{user}}, and do not write the ending.

moveIdeas.name: Move ideas
moveIdeas.instruction: Give 3 numbered one-line candidates for moves {{char}} could make next, in different directions. Do not write lines or the passage.

closeScene.name: Close the scene
closeScene.instruction: Describe what {{char}} says and does to close this scene in a way that reaches the goal of the enabled step. Leave room for {{user}} to reply.

checkVoice.name: Check the voice
checkVoice.instruction: Review the last line of {{char}} against the description and the dialogue examples, and list only the drifts in voice and character. Do not write a fixed line.

roleplay.continue: As {{char}}, continue the flow from where it stopped. Include one action that moves a little toward the goal of the enabled step, and stop where {{user}} can easily reply.

ideas.name: Ideas
ideas.description: Decide the frame in a consultation, produce many ideas in different directions, shake them with objections, then group them into themes and narrow down.
ideas.role: You are {{user}}'s partner for ideas. Speak your mind, question assumptions and bring in examples from other fields. Do not agree with everything, do not anchor on the first idea, and do not cut ideas early for feasibility. {{user}} decides.

frame.name: Frame
frame.goal: In the sub-session, shape what to think about, the trigger, the constraints and the wanted result, and cut the perspectives for ideas into outline steps.

diverge.name: Diverge
diverge.goal: Select a perspective in the outline and produce many ideas in different directions with the command "Generate ideas". When they run out, go to the next perspective.

provoke.name: Provoke
provoke.goal: With the commands "Object" and "Reverse", object to the ideas and dig out hidden assumptions.

converge.name: Converge
converge.goal: Group the ideas with the command "Group into themes", and narrow them down to 2-3 with "Narrow down".

capture.name: Capture
capture.goal: With the command "Capture", write out what was decided, what to check and the open questions.

shapeFrame.name: Shape the frame and perspectives
shapeFrame.greeting:
We will decide the frame of the project and the perspectives for ideas.
Tell me the topic you want to think about, and what you know about the trigger, the constraints and the wanted result.
shapeFrame.instruction:
This is the frame phase of this playbook. Go through the steps below in order; propose for each step, and move on after the user applies it.
1. Frame: shape "what to think about", "trigger", "what is known", "constraints" and "wanted result" for the topic, and fill gaps with up to 5 easy questions. Make the shaped frame a constant individual dictionary entry.
2. Perspectives: offer 3-5 non-overlapping angles for ideas (users, technology, cost, timing, other fields...), and turn the agreed perspectives into outline steps one by one. In each step write what to ask from that perspective (e.g. "What would we drop if the cost were a tenth?").

generate.name: Generate ideas
generate.instruction: Along the frame and the perspective of the enabled step, give 8 numbered ideas. For each, write a short name on the first line, then after a colon the content in one sentence. Vary the scale, method and timing. Do not judge them yet.

objections.name: Object
objections.instruction: Write one objection to each idea so far as a harsh critic. Then name 3 assumptions most ideas make implicitly, and point out the riskiest one.

reverse.name: Reverse
reverse.instruction: List 5 ways to make this problem worse, and give a numbered idea that turns each one around.

themes.name: Group into themes
themes.instruction: Group the ideas so far into themes of similar ones. List the ideas under each theme, and write one line each on "effect for users", "ease of doing", "fit with the goal" and "strength of evidence".

narrow.name: Narrow down
narrow.instruction: Based on the evaluation, give up to 3 numbered recommended ideas. For each, write the name on the first line, then after a colon why you recommend it. Then write the biggest unknown and the cheapest way to check it.

capture.name: Capture
capture.instruction: For the chosen ideas, list "what was decided", "assumptions to check", "open questions", "next actions" and "ideas left out on purpose and why" as bullet points.

ideas.continue: Continuing from there, give ideas or angles that have not come up yet.

research.name: Research
research.description: Decide questions by perspective in a consultation and make them steps, gather what is known per question, summarize with confidence, then check the claims one by one.
research.role: You are a researcher helping {{user}}. Separate what is known from guesses, and say plainly what is uncertain. Do not make up sources. Prefer material {{user}} has pasted.

questions.name: Perspectives and questions
questions.goal: In the sub-session, split the topic into questions by perspective and cut them into outline steps.

gather.name: Gather
gather.goal: Select the question to research in the outline and gather what is known with the command "Answer". Paste material and send it to extract the facts related to the question.

summarize.name: Summarize
summarize.goal: With the command "Summarize", answer the original topic from the questions of the whole outline and what was gathered.

verify.name: Verify
verify.goal: With the command "Verify claims", check the claims of the summary one by one.

makeQuestions.name: Decide perspectives and questions
makeQuestions.greeting:
Let's split the topic into questions by perspective.
Tell me the topic and why you want to know or how you will use it.
makeQuestions.instruction: This is the perspectives and questions phase of this playbook. Show 4-6 perspectives on the topic from different standpoints, list 2-4 questions a person in each would ask, and let the user pick. Turn the chosen questions into outline steps one by one in research order. In each step write the perspective, the question and the level of detail the answer needs.

answer.name: Answer
answer.instruction: Answer the question of the enabled step. First list "what is known", then "guesses" separately, and last "what is uncertain or needs more research". When you use material {{user}} pasted, say which.

summarize.name: Summarize
summarize.instruction: From the answers so far, summarize the answer to the original topic. Write 5-8 findings in order of importance, each with a one-sentence claim, evidence and confidence. Show conflicts as they are without settling them, and write the remaining questions last.

verify.name: Verify claims
verify.instruction: For each claim of the previous summary, pose one question that checks whether it is right, and answer it without looking at the summary. Mark the claims whose answers conflict with the summary.

research.continue: Continue with what you have not yet written about the question of the enabled step.

document.name: Write a document
document.description: Decide everything from the material and readers to the skeleton of chapters and sections in one consultation, make it steps, write section by section, and test as a reader who does not know the background.
document.role: You are a co-author writing a document with {{user}}. Write with the readers and what should happen after reading in mind. Do not fill unknowns with guesses; ask.

prepare.name: Preparation
prepare.goal: In the sub-session, gather the kind of document, the readers, what should happen after reading and the material, and cut the skeleton of chapters and sections into the outline.

sections.name: Write by section
sections.goal: Select the section to write in the outline and write it with the command "Write the section". You can pick the contents with "Content ideas".

readerTest.name: Reader test
readerTest.goal: Look for holes as a reader who does not know the background with the command "Reader questions", and review against the whole outline with "Review it through".

makePlan.name: Decide material to skeleton
makePlan.greeting:
Let's gather the material for the document and decide everything up to the skeleton of chapters and sections.
Tell me the kind of document, the readers and what should happen after reading, and paste the material you have.
makePlan.instruction:
This is the preparation phase of this playbook. Go through the steps below in order; propose for each step, and move on after the user applies it.
1. Material: read the pasted material, sum up "kind", "readers", "what should happen after reading" and "constraints" briefly, and ask 5-10 questions that can be answered briefly about what is missing. Propose the summed-up material as an item before the session history.
2. Skeleton: show the skeleton of chapters and sections from the material and agree on it, then turn the sections into outline steps one by one in writing order. In each step write the goal of the chapter it belongs to, what the section tells and what the reader should keep. Do not write the text yet.

writeSection.name: Write the section
writeSection.instruction: Write the text of the section of the enabled step. Use only the chosen candidates if any, otherwise choose from the material. Keep the wording consistent with the previous sections.

contentIdeas.name: Content ideas
contentIdeas.instruction: Give 8 numbered one-line candidates for contents of the section of the enabled step. Put those in the material first, and those not in the material after them, marked "not in the material".

readerQuestions.name: Reader questions
readerQuestions.instruction: List 5-10 numbered questions a first-time reader of this document would likely ask, and answer each only from the text of the document. Mark questions it cannot answer, places likely to be misread, and conflicts.

reviewAll.name: Review it through
reviewAll.instruction: Read the text so far through, and list breaks in the flow, repetitions, conflicts and empty sentences as bullet points. Show only the places to fix.

document.continue: Continue the section of the enabled step. Keep the wording consistent with the previous paragraphs.

twist.name: Change the course
twist.instruction: In the next passage, make one event happen that changes the course so far. Do not contradict the story so far or the settled setting.

accident.name: Chance event
accident.instruction: Mix one small chance event that nobody expected into the next passage.

assumptions.name: Question an assumption
assumptions.instruction: Name one assumption taken for granted in the last exchange, and write what would change if it failed.

plain.name: Say it simply
plain.instruction: Restate the last answer in short sentences without technical terms.

changeScene.name: Change the scene
changeScene.instruction: Move in time or place and start a new scene. Show the move in one sentence, then continue.

playbook.candidatesFailed: Could not read candidates from this response
playbook.ownEmpty: Copy one to make your own; it appears here.
playbook.allHidden: All are hidden in the Features tab.
playbook.deleteBody: "{name}" is removed from your list. Chats that use it keep their copy.

editor.title: Playbook
editor.name: Name
editor.role: Role text (what the assistant does and does not do)
editor.noSendTo: The action to send with is gone

scope.decide: Done in a consultation. Only the phase text is sent to the chat
scope.proceed: Done in the chat. Sends: the phase text and the enabled steps
scope.close: Done in the chat. Sends: the phase text and the enabled steps (all after Show all)

editor.writesOutline: Have it write the prompt of each step into the outline
editor.revise: Put in the input box (regenerate rewrites the last passage)

received.title: Received data
received.truncated: Shortened in the middle because it is large

entry.title: Set API key
entry.invalidUrl: Enter a base URL that starts with http:// or https://.
